study_scope: Completed boundary-form, normal/gradient component, mean/oscillation, spatial-mode/frequency and cold finite-support forced-FVM controls; developed production force comparison.
production_intervention: none; manual healthy case preserved; no new drag_recovery files

findings.finding: The mature planar force deficit persists with negligible cycle-to-cycle recovery.

The native mixed Un/Gt plus fixedFluxPressure condition transmits almost all reference force amplitude on the actual small FVM mesh when supplied with exact reference boundary data. Full-velocity imposition does not improve its response to the same actual VPM input.

Replacing only normal-velocity oscillation substantially changes forces. Replacing only the normal derivative of tangential velocity does not. The influential mismatch enters through the unsteady normal-velocity channel.
Both the normal spatial coefficients/initial force-relative phase and its frequency affect the response. There is no single global velocity-amplitude scaling that represents this error.
findings.strength: two-by-two controlled mode/frequency substitution; finite settling

findings.finding: Discarding the same cold reference coefficients outside production VPM bounds causes a substantial drag-amplitude reduction, with little lift change. Full/cropped instantaneous image controls do not establish autonomous recovery.
The measured support change alters side-face fundamental amplitude, phase and spatial distribution. A distinct second-harmonic input attenuation was not found.
Freestream, physical viscosity, planar span/circulation/volume scaling and clock ratios are correct in the examined native path.
One complete-support M4 scatter on this frozen developed wall-free wake has little aggregate field loss. This does not exclude wall, renewal or repeated evolving feedback effects.
findings.strength: conditional frozen operator, no flow advanced

remaining_localization: The native VPM operation responsible for the remaining autonomous lift/waveform deficit has not been uniquely isolated. Transfer/near-wall representation and evolving wake feedback remain distinct hypotheses. No stronger boundary model or numerical repair has been demonstrated to recover mature autonomous Cd/Cl.
recommended_correction_direction: Preserve the mixed velocity/vorticity boundary condition and correct the VPM field supplied to it. The demonstrated finite-support error warrants retaining the remote wake induction rather than silently deleting its contribution: first test larger retention support, then a conservative resolved/coarsened far-wake representation with explicit induced-field error control if cost requires it. Do not retune freestream, force coefficients, forcing frequency or phase to match plots.
required_fix_qualification: A self-sustained coupled control must show mature complete Cd/Cl cycles, correct phase/frequency/velocity fields and finite compatible native checkpoints at unchanged tolerances. Check comparable resources/particle population and measured phase timings; source/clock/linear-solver success alone is not force recovery.
limitations: Each twelve-second forced control has only one complete lift cycle in102–112s; reported response does not prove settled autonomous saturation.
Mode substitutions alter spatial amplitude distribution and initial force-relative phase together; they do not separately identify a unique spatial/phase mechanism.
Mean-only controls do not eliminate indirect mean-flow effects in the closed coupled feedback loop.

The cold reference image is approximate, not an exact full-vorticity oracle. All301 independent images were admitted by the unchanged native closure and strength/capacity guards; retired warm images are excluded.
The isolated wall-support correction did not recover amplitudes in its12s continuation and remains unpromoted.
Native physics and rollback checks exclude the demonstrated faults only within their recorded scope.
Mean lift is close to zero; a ratio of mean lift is not meaningful and is deliberately omitted.
